findings.evidence: "Then, the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email."
findings.fix: Remove this paragraph or rewrite it as a clear statement of the intended approval workflow (e.g., "The designated manager or their designated backup reviewer reviews and approves the request").
findings.location: How to Apply section, third paragraph
findings.violation: This paragraph reads like documentation of a specific incident rather than a policy statement. It describes a current failure scenario instead of the intended approval process.

findings.evidence: "The manager approves items pursuant to internal discretion, notwithstanding the standard review checklist."
findings.fix: Either remove the phrase to make the checklist mandatory, or explicitly state what discretion the manager has and the conditions under which they can deviate from the checklist.
findings.violation: The phrase "notwithstanding the standard review checklist" is ambiguous about whether managers can override the checklist, contradicting the Approval Timeline section which states the manager "confirms the equipment category matches the approved list."

findings.evidence: "Also, the deposit happens in order to offset costs the employee already paid at this point in time."
findings.violation: This sentence is redundant (reimbursement inherently offsets already-paid costs) and uses unnecessary phrasing. It adds no substantive policy information.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite as "Employees must keep their equipment in good working condition and the company may request a photo check once a year."
findings.location: Restrictions and Exceptions section, first sentence
findings.violation: The document uses consistent third-person language throughout (employees, managers, staff) but shifts to direct address here ("You must," "we may"), creating inconsistent voice and formality.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form" and "you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there"
findings.fix: Rewrite as "Employees record the stipend item on the request form" and "Employees submit the request in the portal and track its status there."
findings.location: Terminology Notes section, first and second paragraphs
findings.violation: Inconsistent voice: the document uses third-person throughout but switches to direct address ("You") in this section only.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Provide a complete, numbered list of all required steps to submit a stipend request.
findings.violation: This section lists only two items with minimal detail, contradicting the earlier statement that "The portal walks through each step in order." No complete step list is provided.

findings.evidence: "Program Overview" at the start states "The people operations office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter"; later "Overview" section states "The benefits team publishes the reimbursement log after every open enrollment period."
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate "Overview" section and consolidate all overview information in the "Program Overview" section, clarifying which team publishes and the exact schedule.
findings.location: Document structure - Overview section appears twice
findings.violation: A section titled "Overview" appears after "Request Steps," duplicating and contradicting the "Program Overview" section with different responsible parties and publication schedules.
